target_customer: Adults with irritable bowel syndrome, reached as consumers or through health systems (the launch post claims pilots at health systems)
problem: IBS affects an estimated 15 to 20 percent of people; diet changes such as low-FODMAP work in trials but are hard to follow without expert guidance.
business_model: Digital therapeutic with coaching, subscription or health-system contracts (not specified in sources)
product_category: Digital therapeutic for IBS and digestive health

founders.name: Lauren Kelley-Chew
prior_employers: Healthcare investing (firm not named in source)
founders.background_notes: Per the Launch HN post (2018-04-25): Lauren and Luke are siblings and Lauren is an MD from UPenn who previously worked in healthcare investing.

founders.name: Luke Kelley-Chew
founders.background_notes: Per the Launch HN post, Luke went into tech and then business school.

exit.reason: No public statement found; YC marks the company Inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: A messaging-based coaching app that personalizes a low-FODMAP program from user data; the clinical validation, not the software, was the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Low-FODMAP coaching content is widely available and no proprietary clinical evidence was found; a third-party review said the first clinically proven claim lacked a trial, publication or regulatory submission.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Digital IBS programs from other companies (Mahana, Cara Care, metaMe) later won regulatory clearances and funding; nothing indicates they copied or acquired Caelum.

market_need_then: IBS is common, and the founders cited trial evidence for diet and lifestyle changes; the launch post claimed pilots at 7 of the top 10 health systems but no independent verification was found.

branding.domain_note: caelumhealth.com could not be fetched in this session (host not allowed), and a directory says the domain now belongs to someone else.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical positioning (claimed first clinically proven digital treatment for IBS); the homepage later moved to a diet coaching message per one directory

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage found beyond a Hacker News launch post and directories; the name resembles Caelus Health and other Caelum companies.

outcome_analysis: The cause of the shutdown is not public. The two founders launched a digital IBS therapeutic from YC Summer 2017, publicly launched on Hacker News in April 2018, and are now Inactive. A directory page says the cause was no product-market fit but gives no sourcing, so it is not used. No funding was found, so no failure factor is assigned.
notes: Founder facts come from a blog repost of the Launch HN post; the original thread was not opened. Search results for funding returned other IBS companies (metaMe Health, Mahana, HiDoc) which are not Caelum. The caelumhealth.com fetch failed with a DNS error, indicating the host is outside the allowed network or not resolving, so the site could not be checked. Competitor list is empty: the launch post names no competitors, and the IBS digital therapeutic rivals found (Mahana, Cara Care, metaMe) have funding and clearance news dated after 2018 only.
